newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Insurance companies must pay in EU asbestos case.
newsitem.headline: Insurance companies must pay in EU asbestos case.

text.p: Europe's high court on Thursday ordered insurance companies to pay out 26 million Belgian francs in the first case relating to claims by European Union civil servants that they contracted cancer from asbestos used in the European Commission's old Berlaymont headquarters building.

The insurance companies, including Royale Belge of Belgium and Assurances Generales de France (AGF), had contested a decision by the European Commission, the EU's executive, to compensate one former employee for lung cancer alleged to have been caused by the asbestos.
Olivier Eben, a lawyer acting for a number of the victims, told Reuters the European Court of Justice's decision opened the way for further compensation claims.

"There are around 64 cases that we know of, but there could be much more," Eben said. At least two former civil servants have already died from asbestos-related diseases, and at least one family is seeking damages, he added.
A European Commission spokesman said only three claims were in their final stages or had been settled.
The distinctive star-shaped Berlaymont housed around 3,000 European civil servants until the end of 1991 when it was evacuated following a report into the health threat posed by the asbestos.
The building is currently shrouded in white plastic as part of a multi-billion Belgian franc clean up and refurbishment aimed at rehousing the Commission by the year 2000.
A spokesman for Royale Belge was not immediately available to comment on the European court ruling.
